title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: usage-based billing models in the model selector
notes: claim 57: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the briefing implies credit requests arrive with initial model access, omits the required Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription licence, and gives misleading visibility and data-boundary assurances. The Graph entry is not an actionable operation, and one admin control is linked to the wrong documentation and described as governing visibility when it governs access requests.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is in development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap product is Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365).
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The listed platforms are Desktop and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists December CY2026 for General Availability.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"
claims.fix: Keep December CY2026 as a roadmap target, and add the supplied notice's more specific window: MC1519122, updated November 4, expects Worldwide GA to begin early December 2026 and complete by mid-December 2026. Cite https://admin.microsoft.com/Adminportal/Home#/MessageCenter/:/messages/MC1519122 as a message-center source.

claims.claim: Preview is listed for November CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "November CY2026"
claims.fix: Retain the roadmap target and add MC1519122's Frontier (Public) rollout window: beginning early November 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026. Cite the supplied notice rather than reporting only the month.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on November 4, 2026.
Users will be able to access usage-based billing models through the Chat model selector.
claims.quote: Users will be able to access models that require usage-based billing (UBB) from the model selector in Chat.

claims.claim: Access to these UBB models requires administrator enablement, so the default state is admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: Users will not have access to UBB models unless UBB is enabled.

claims.claim: Tenant administrators need to provide credits for users to interact with the models.
claims.quote: Tenant admins will need to allocate credits so that users can interact with these models.

claims.claim: In-product requests for additional credits are part of the initial model-selector rollout.
claims.quote: After the initial rollout, we plan to roll out the ability for users to request additional credits from their tenant admin.
claims.fix: Separate model access from credit requests in the summary, body and rollout guidance. Say that MC1519122 plans in-product additional-credit requests after the initial rollout, without a date; communicate the organisation's interim request process.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: UBB frontier-model usage consumes Copilot Credits beyond the everyday AI covered by the per-user subscription.
claims.quote: UBB is used for advanced AI and frontier models, extending beyond the everyday AI included in the USL.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/user-subscription-license-usage-based-billing to sources for the USL/UBB distinction. Retain the consumption licensing model and variable cost rating.

claims.claim: Enabled UBB and a covering spending policy are sufficient prerequisites for Copilot Chat users to access the models.
claims.quote: Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL) with UBB enabled
claims.fix: Add the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription licence requirement to Scope and licensing.notes. State that enabled UBB and credits are additional requirements, not an alternative to the USL. Cite MC1519122 and https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/user-subscription-license-usage-based-billing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Cost Management billing framework supports pay-as-you-go, Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plan (P3), and existing prepaid capacity packs.
claims.quote: Enable usage-based billing with flexible options including Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3), pay-as-you-go, or existing prepaid capacity packs.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: Spending policies allocate credits to users.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.
claims.fix: Replace 'allocate credits through spending policies' with 'enable UBB, provide credits, and configure access and spending limits through spending policies'. Preserve the roadmap's credit-provision requirement without describing limits as reserved allocations.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Having no spending policy hides the metered models from users.
claims.quote: In short, this setting controls visibility, while Cost Management under the Copilot node in the Microsoft 365 admin center controls access and spending.
claims.fix: Replace the hiding guarantee with 'Without enabled UBB and credits, users cannot use these models.' Explain that discovery and requests are distinct from spending access; the discovery setting is deprecated. Leave Chat-specific hidden-versus-disabled appearance as an open question.

claims.claim: Users cannot consume UBB experiences before administrators configure billing.
claims.quote: Admins must set up a billing policy before a user can use AI experiences that require usage-based billing.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: UBB spending policy configuration is in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration.
claims.quote: Select Manage Configuration. The Configuration tab within the Cost management page is displayed.

claims.claim: /beta/copilot/costManagement (Cost Management API) is an actionable Graph call for spending policies, limits and alerts.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies Graph API PowerShell create billing policy. Opened Cost Management API overview and List spendingPolicies; the root namespace is described, but no HTTP operation matching the printed methodless call is documented.
claims.fix: Use a real operation with its specific purpose, such as 'GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies' to list policies. Link https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/spendingpolicy-list. State that beta APIs can change and are unsupported in production; GET does not configure limits or alerts.

claims.claim: The cited setup page documents Copilot > Settings > All Settings > Access to usage-based billing experiences as a visibility control.
claims.quote: Your selection controls who can request access. It does not complete the usage-based billing setup by itself.
claims.fix: The path exists, but not on its cited setup page and not for the stated purpose. Rename governs to 'Who can request access to usage-based billing experiences', retain the path, and set docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/request-access-usage-based-billing-experiences. Do not equate denying requests with hiding models.

claims.claim: No API equivalent for the Access to usage-based billing experiences request setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Access to usage-based billing experiences" "API". Opened UBB setup, discovery-setting-ai-experiences, request-access-usage-based-billing-experiences and Cost Management API overview; no automation equivalent for the request setting found.

claims.claim: Anthropic access can be scoped to users through Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Anthropic and its user-choice setting.
claims.quote: select Copilot > Settings > View all. ... Select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors. ... select Anthropic, and Save. ... Under Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences, select your users or groups and Save.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: Anthropic opt-in prose
claims.claim: No published API or PowerShell equivalent was found for the Anthropic subprocessor opt-in.
claims.quote: Searched: "Anthropic" "PowerShell" "subprocessor"; "Anthropic" "subprocessor" "Graph API"; "Anthropic" "subprocessor" "API" "setting". Opened connect-to-ai-subprocessor and copilot-anthropic-apps; both document portal controls, not an automation equivalent.

claims.claim: The general Copilot services pay-as-you-go surface is Copilot > Billing & usage > Pay-as-you-go services.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Billing & usage. Select the Pay-as-you-go services tab, then select Microsoft Copilot Chat or SharePoint agent.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent was found for the general Copilot services pay-as-you-go billing policy control.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies Graph API PowerShell create billing policy; "Copilot" "pay-as-you-go" "billing policies" "API". Opened capacity-packs and Cost Management API overview; spending-policy APIs do not document this separate billing-policy setup.

claims.claim: The older Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go billing-policy surface governs this UBB frontier-model selector feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "UBB models" "billing policy"; Copilot pay-as-you-go billing policies Graph API PowerShell create billing policy. Opened capacity-packs, UBB overview, setup and USL/UBB guidance; none maps the older Copilot Chat billing-policy surface to these frontier models.
claims.fix: Remove this row from the feature-specific controls, or add a note: 'General Copilot Chat billing control; Microsoft has not confirmed that this surface configures UBB frontier-model access.' Direct feature deployment to the UBB Cost Management setup identified by MC1519122.

claims.claim: No separate administrative switch for the Chat UBB model selector is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Chat" "model selector" "admin" "hide"; Copilot Chat model selector admin hide models no policy default credit request routing administrators. Opened setup, discovery and access-request settings; no separate Chat UBB selector switch found.
claims.fix: Replace the absolute statement with 'A separate Chat UBB model-selector switch was not found in the Microsoft documentation reviewed in November 2026.' Add a both-null control row for that documented gap, without applying Cowork-only model templates to Chat.

claims.claim: Disabling Anthropic as a provider removes users' option to use Claude models.
claims.quote: Once you disable Anthropic as an AI subprocessor, users won't have the option to use Claude models.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls: credit-request path
claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Credit requests is the documented direct approval path on Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: From the Top Actions section, you can View requests and Manage spending policies
claims.fix: Give the full documented route: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Overview > View requests, opening Credit requests. Replace the manage-copilot-credits link with https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending#viewing-and-managing-credit-requests. Qualify feature-specific availability using MC1519122.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: request routing
claims.claim: The Cost Management framework supports custom routing policies for credit requests.
claims.quote: Configure request-routing policies for supported credit requests.

claims.claim: Without routing policies credit requests land on a default administrator audience.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "credit requests" "default" "administrators"; Copilot Chat model selector admin hide models no policy default credit request routing administrators. Opened UBB overview, setup and Monitor Copilot Credit spending; no default recipient audience is specified.
claims.fix: Replace with 'Requests that do not match a custom request policy continue through the Microsoft credit request service and can be resolved in the Microsoft 365 admin center.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Identity-based spending policies govern service access through users and groups, including group membership.
claims.quote: At this time, you can only support specific users and resource accounts through security groups.

claims.claim: Administrators can configure monthly policy-level credit limits.
claims.quote: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Administrators can set optional monthly per-user credit limits.
claims.quote: In the Select the monthly spending limit for users (optional) section, set a monthly limit for users to prevent a single person from spending all available credits.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Policy and user-level threshold alerts can warn as configured limits approach.
claims.quote: User-level notifications alert users as they approach their spending limit. The user-level notifications are separate from notifications sent to administrators or stakeholders about overall policy consumption.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Consumption tab provides reporting by spending policy, user, group, agent and service.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab enables detailed analysis by spending policy, user, group, agent, or service.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription supplies a fixed-price foundation for everyday AI.
claims.quote: The USL covers everyday AI work, providing a fixed-price AI foundation for your workforce.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/user-subscription-license-usage-based-billing. Describe the ongoing USL/UBB distinction, not a claim that all Copilot work was exclusively fixed-price until this release.

claims.claim: Until this release users could not choose the model behind Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: Users can now select Claude as a model option in Copilot Chat for complex analysis, document understanding, and structured content generation.
claims.fix: Remove 'the model behind it was Microsoft's choice'. Say 'This change adds usage-based frontier models alongside existing subscription-covered model choices.' The cited June 16, 2026 release notes already document user model choice.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Credit consumption varies with the model used and the work performed.
claims.quote: The number of credits a task consumes varies with the models used, the amount of context retrieved, the runtime needed to plan and complete the work, and the tools the task calls.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Model choice introduces no change to the Microsoft 365 data boundary.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings such as Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary
claims.fix: Remove the blanket assurance from the data-exposure bullet and risk rationale. State that Claude models are excluded from the EU Data Boundary and applicable in-country processing commitments; assess the selected model's processing terms before enablement.

claims.claim: All selectable models keep prompts and Graph data under the same Copilot contractual commitments.
claims.quote: This means data is stored by Anthropic and not subject to your Microsoft Customer Agreement including commitments in the Product Terms and DPA.
claims.fix: Qualify the assurance by model and tenant eligibility. Claude models supplied with Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor use Microsoft's applicable terms; separately enabled models labelled 'Anthropic models with Data Retention' use Anthropic's separate terms. Do not assume all Fable-class models have identical terms.

claims.claim: Dashboard totals can be point-in-time views rather than finalized billing figures.
claims.quote: It's not the same as an invoice view. Dashboard totals and exports might be point-in-time views and can refresh at different intervals.

claims.claim: The Cost Management operational view is expressed in credits rather than currency.
claims.quote: Everything in this view is expressed in Copilot Credits, not currency.

claims.claim: Copilot Credit P3 is an annual commitment.
claims.quote: Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans provide discounted commit units for eligible Copilot Credit usage during a one-year term.

claims.claim: Pre-purchased annual credits provide discounts compared with pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Pre-purchasing annual credits provides discounted rates compared to pay-as-you-go pricing.

claims.claim: Usage beyond P3 credits continues on pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: any usage beyond your prepaid credits automatically continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.claim: Global Administrators and Billing Administrators manage Cost Management billing methods.
claims.quote: Global administrator and Billing administrator roles can add, select, and change billing methods, and set billing methods in policies.

claims.claim: AI Administrators and License Administrators can manage spending-policy limits and alerts.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: Supported reader roles can review consumption information.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.

claims.claim: Spending policies can automatically include future supported services.
claims.quote: Review the Auto-apply new services setting. This setting is turned on by default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Feature-specific credit rates per Chat UBB model were not found in the reviewed Microsoft documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat UBB models model selector credit rates published GPT-6 Astra Claude Fable subscription USL; "Chat" "Astra" "credits" "rate"; "UBB" "models" "credit rates". Opened USL/UBB, UBB overview, setup and billing comparison; no Chat model rate table found.

claims.claim: The roadmap description does not name the models or their credit rates.
claims.quote: Users will be able to access models that require usage-based billing (UBB) from the model selector in Chat.

claims.claim: Which models will be metered in this rollout is still an unanswered question.
claims.quote: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 will be generally available as UBB models with this rollout. Previously communicated eligibility requirements for these models apply.
claims.fix: Name GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 as the models announced in MC1519122, retaining the notice's eligibility qualification. Keep only the unpublished credit rates as an open question.

claims.claim: No government-cloud rollout dates for this specific roadmap feature were found.
claims.quote: Searched: "571400" "GCC"; Copilot Chat UBB models model selector credit rates published GPT-6 Astra Claude Fable subscription USL. Read roadmap, MC1519122, UBB overview and Anthropic regional exclusions; none gives government dates for this Chat UBB rollout.

claims.claim: Billed amounts appear in Azure Cost Management.
claims.quote: Azure Cost Management shows pay-as-you-go charges and purchase or amortized cost information for Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans (P3)
claims.fix: Qualify this as Azure-subscription pay-as-you-go charges and P3 purchase/amortized costs. Add that Azure Cost Management does not show consumption against prepaid capacity packs, which is monitored in the applicable Microsoft 365 or Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: The new model options will be visible to every Copilot Chat user after rollout.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Chat" "model selector" "admin" "hide"; Copilot Chat model selector admin hide models no policy default credit request routing administrators. Read MC1519122, discovery and access-request settings; none guarantees visibility to every Chat user.
claims.fix: Remove 'Visible to every Copilot Chat user'. Say that eligible, licensed users with UBB enabled and credits gain additional model choices; the hidden-versus-disabled experience for other users is not established. Reassess the impact rationale without a universal-visibility premise.

claims.where: Governance guidance: request routing; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist directs administrators to configure credit-request routing, but the controls table has no routing row.
claims.quote: Design credit request routing so requests reach a team that can judge them. | The controls table lists spending policies, UBB experiences, Anthropic access and pay-as-you-go billing, but not routing.
claims.fix: Add a credit-request routing row: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Overview > View requests > Request policies > Add request policy. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending#configure-custom-request-policies and qualify availability for this rollout.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The page treats policyless model visibility both as hidden and as visible but unusable.
claims.quote: Users can only see and use these models if a tenant administrator has allocated credits | the model selector will show options that most users cannot use until a policy covers them | Whether administrators can hide the metered options
claims.fix: Use one consistent statement: enabled UBB and credits govern use; the appearance for users without access is not established. Remove both the guaranteed hiding and guaranteed visibility claims, and retain the Chat-specific appearance question.
